title: XMPP Stanza Anatomy (RFC 6120): Parsing & Constructing Stanzas
solutionExplanation:
The solution implements binary string scanning and XML construction:
1. classify_xml_packet detects top-level tag names (stream:stream, auth, iq, presence, message) and extracts attributes using extract_attr.
2. extract_attr supports both single-quote ('val') and double-quote ("val") delimiters without string escape ambiguity, returning binary:copy/1 to prevent memory pinning.
3. build_stream_features, build_bind_result, and build_chat_message use IO lists (iolist_to_binary/1) to assemble wire XML with zero-copy efficiency.

mentalModelCheck.question: Why does an XMPP <iq type="get"> stanza strictly require the recipient to return an <iq type="result"> or <iq type="error"> with the exact same id attribute?

options.label: To enable asynchronous request-response RPC matching over the persistent stream without head-of-line blocking.
options.explanation: Because stanzas are multiplexed asynchronously over a single TCP stream, the client uses the unique id attribute to match responses to requests.

options.label: Because Erlang processes will crash if the id is missing.
options.explanation: It is an RFC 6120 protocol specification requirement for multiplexed RPC correlation.

options.label: To encrypt the payload for privacy.
options.explanation: The id attribute provides correlation, not encryption.

options.label: Because the XML parser cannot parse closing tags without an id.
options.explanation: XML parsers do not require id attributes to parse closing tags.
